# Visualize -- Agent API

> Visualize is a browser-based, audio-reactive VJ mixer built on the
> Noisemaker engine. It runs two decks, A and B. Each deck runs a Noisemaker
> DSL program. A crossfader and a mixer effect blend the decks into the
> output. The Visualize agent API lets a software agent read, check and run
> deck programs, use the library, crossfader, mixer, effects, automation,
> tempo and scenes, and look at the output. This file is the contract for
> software agents that control Visualize.

The full contract adds a reference for every command and its arguments:
https://visualize.noisedeck.app/llms-full.txt

The DSL itself (syntax, effects, parameters, surfaces) is specified by the
Noisemaker contract: https://noisemaker.app/llms-full.txt

For the roles and control paths of the other Noise Factor products,
including Timeline's project-folder CLI and Layers' separate document, start
from the platform guide at https://noisefactor.io/llms.txt.

## Connect

Visualize runs in the person's browser. Use the first route that you can use.

### 1. Through the person's online session (agents with a shell)

This route controls the Visualize tab that the person already has open, with
their audio, decks and output. It needs a shell with Node.js 22.4 or later.

1. Ask the person to open https://visualize.noisedeck.app/, click
   **connect agent...** beside the Seance button in the top bar, then
   **Go Online**, then **Copy Prompt**, and paste the prompt to you. The prompt
   names this contract and the session link. The button is not offered in a
   tab that joined someone else's session. (Without that button: the Seance
   button, whose tooltip is "Collaborate online", then **Take Online**, then
   send you the session code that the dialog shows after "Online", or the
   session URL that **Copy URL** copies.)
2. Get the agent tool and join the session:

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://noisedeck.app/agent/seance-agent.mjs
node seance-agent.mjs join <code-or-url>
node seance-agent.mjs commands
```

`join` prints the session. Its name is the app name, `visualize`. `commands`
lists every Visualize command with its arguments. Commands marked
`[not available remotely]` fail with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` through a session
(see "How it works" below).

3. Run commands. Commands that act on one deck take `{"deck":"B"}`; deck A
   is the default.

```sh
node seance-agent.mjs call getState
node seance-agent.mjs call setCrossfader '{"position":0.5}'
node seance-agent.mjs program                       # deck A program text
node seance-agent.mjs program --doc deck:B          # deck B program text
node seance-agent.mjs validate program.dsl          # check a program file
node seance-agent.mjs set program.dsl               # run it on deck A
node seance-agent.mjs set --args '{"deck":"B"}' program.dsl
node seance-agent.mjs look                          # image of the output
node seance-agent.mjs look --args '{"source":"B"}'  # image of deck B
node seance-agent.mjs wait --doc deck:B --since <rev>
node seance-agent.mjs image-put photo.png           # result.ref is image:<sha256>
node seance-agent.mjs leave
```

`look` saves the image as a file; its path is
`result.envelope.result.image.path`. Images travel as bytes; the tool never
prints image data. `program --json` adds the document
revision for `wait --since`. `set` and `validate` read `-` as standard input.
Output is JSON except the program text and the `commands` list (`commands
--json` gives JSON). A result drops the state snapshot
unless you add `--state`.

The session has two documents: `deck:A` (the default) and `deck:B`. A
program that a deck runs is in its document, so people in the session see
your changes. `wait` returns when a person changes deck A's program; add
`--doc deck:B` to watch deck B.

To move a program and its images between apps, join both sessions and use
`transfer`. Name the deck with `--from-args` or `--to-args`:

```sh
node seance-agent.mjs transfer noisedeck visualize --to-args '{"deck":"B"}'
node seance-agent.mjs transfer visualize noisedeck --from-args '{"deck":"A"}'
```

The tool exits with 0 when the command succeeded, 1 when Visualize answered
with `ok: false` (read `result.envelope.error.code`), and 2 when the tool
itself could not run the command (read `error.code`; the codes are listed
below). `node seance-agent.mjs help` lists every option.

How it works, so you can explain it to the person:

- The tool joins the session as an anonymous participant, which the person
  sees join. It runs commands in the tab that took the set online, through
  the session, with the same checks as the person's own controls. No other
  tab answers, even one that becomes the session's owner after the person's
  tab leaves. After a reload, the person's tab answers again.
- Everyone in the session receives every answer, and anyone who can edit the
  session can send commands to that tab. So what this browser stores for the
  person is not reachable through a session: `listScenes`, `scene`,
  `listUserEffects` and `setAutoVjPool` answer `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`; the
  library's `user` section and `user` effects are left out of `searchLibrary`,
  `searchEffects` and `getEffectDefinition`; a program that names the `user`
  namespace anywhere fails with a `USER_EFFECT` diagnostic; `randomize` picks
  from the whole library except utility and `user` programs, not from the
  person's Auto-VJ pool; and `setAutoVj` cannot turn Auto-VJ on, because
  Auto-VJ draws from that pool (it can turn it off and set its cycle).
- Changes through a session are live but are not stored as the person's
  settings: the crossfade curve, the mixer effect and its parameters, the
  rebind options, Auto-Mix on or off and its source, the tempo divider and
  following the MIDI clock keep the values the person stored.
- What Visualize keeps out of the session stays out: `getProgram` and the
  state snapshot describe the text that the session holds for a deck, not an
  unpublished draft; `getThumbnail` answers `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` for a deck
  that can show live camera or video pixels (from the moment its source first
  shows until the deck runs a program without `media()`, because a `media()`
  program keeps showing the last frame after its source stops), for the output
  while either deck can, and for a frozen output that froze while one could;
  and `setProgram` accepts only images that the session already holds.
- Commands that act on the person's browser rather than on the performance
  answer `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`: `setAudioInput`, `setMidiInput`, `setAudio`
  (input sensitivity), `setRenderer` and `record`. `commands` marks every
  command that a session cannot run. The live decks, the crossfader and mixer,
  the effects, automation and tempo, and the built-in and curated library stay
  reachable. Suggest that the person goes offline when you are done (the
  Seance button, then **Go Offline**).
- Images cross a session only as bytes. A request or an answer that would carry
  an image as base64 text fails with `IMAGE_AS_TEXT`, and a request that names
  media by an outside link, which would make the person's browser fetch it,
  fails with `OUTSIDE_LINK`.
- `look` asks the person's tab for an image of the output or a deck. The tab
  adds the image to the session as its own bytes, and the tool saves it as a
  file.
- A session holds at most 32 images, and the person's own images need room
  too. The tab takes at most 16 images in ten minutes; past that, `look`
  answers `IMAGE_LIMIT` with `details.retryAfter` in seconds. Look when the
  output has changed, not in a loop.

Agent tool errors (exit code 2, `error.code`):

- `NO_SESSION`: no session is joined, or more than one and none was named.
- `UNKNOWN_SESSION`, `SESSION_LOCKED`, `REFUSED`: the session code is wrong or
  expired, the session is locked, or the session refused the join.
- `NO_APP_TAB`: the tab that took the session online did not answer. Ask the
  person to keep it open, or to go online again and send the new code.
- `TIMEOUT`: the tab did not answer in time. Check `status`, then try again.
- `READONLY`: the session lets this agent only read the program text:
  `program`, `wait` and `status` work, and every app command, `commands` and
  `look` included, is refused. Ask the person to allow guests to edit.
- `SESSION_CLOSED`, `SESSION_REFUSED`: the connection closed, or the session
  server refused a request (the message says why).
- `ISLAND`: a `transfer` to or from a Layers session. Layers shares nothing
  with the other apps.
- `IMAGE_FAILED`, `NO_DOCUMENT`, `USAGE`, `INVALID_JSON`: an image transfer
  failed, a document is missing, or the command line was wrong.
- `CONNECT_FAILED`, `RATE_LIMITED`: `join` could not reach the session server,
  or the server is limiting joins from this address. Wait a minute, then join
  again.
- `INVALID_IMAGE`, `BAD_RESPONSE`: an image id is malformed, or the app sent
  an answer that the tool could not read.
- `DAEMON_FAILED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`: the tool's background process did not
  start, or the tool failed. If it happens again, run `stop` and join again.
- A file that the tool cannot read gives the system's code, such as `ENOENT`.

### 2. WebMCP (browser tools)

Open https://visualize.noisedeck.app/ and discover the page tools named
`visualize_getState`, `visualize_setProgram`, and so on. Each tool has the
argument schema in the reference below and returns the envelope as text.
`visualize_getThumbnail` also returns an image content block, without
duplicating its bytes in text. If your harness serializes the whole tool
result, parse it, display the image through your image tool, and print only
the text block. Do not print image bytes.

### 3. Page JavaScript

Call `window.VisualizeAgent` directly. Wait until the object and the method
exist. Every command waits for startup; awaiting `window.VisualizeAgent.ready`
also works. Return the fields you need, not the whole API object.

```js
const env = await window.VisualizeAgent.getProgram({ deck: 'B' })
return env.result.dsl
```

All routes run the same commands, one at a time, with the same validation.
Only the browser routes run the commands that a session cannot run. WebMCP
availability depends on the browser; if discovery returns no tools, use page
JavaScript. Do not try to bypass a browser tool's read-only JavaScript policy.
A tool that only fetches HTML cannot run Visualize: it needs a browser with
WebGL2. In a small window or with a shared program link, Visualize first
shows a start card. Commands wait until the person (or you) clicks
`start set`, or a deck button on a shared link.

---

## Two decks and the output

- Deck A and deck B each run one program. `getProgram`, `setProgram`,
  `loadProgram`, `randomize`, `setDeck` and `rebind` take `deck`.
- The crossfader `position` runs from 0 (deck A) to 1 (deck B). The live deck
  is A below 0.5 and B from 0.5. The mixer effect (`getMixer`, `setMixer`)
  blends the decks; the crossfader drives its `driver` parameter.
- Output effects (`setFx`) act on the mixed output. `getThumbnail` returns the
  output by default, or one deck with `source`.
- Auto-VJ (`setAutoVj`) loads library programs into the deck that is not live
  and fades to them. Auto-Mix (`setAutoMix`) moves the crossfader from one
  source. Only one of them runs at a time. Both change the decks or the
  crossfader without commands from you; read `state` to follow them.
- The tempo (`setTempo`) sets the deck loop length: one loop is `divider` bars.
- A scene (`scene`, `listScenes`) stores both decks and the whole mixer state
  in this browser. Scene commands run only in the browser, not through a
  session.

## Write a program

1. Find effects with `searchEffects`. Read their parameters with
   `getEffectDefinition`. Library programs (`searchLibrary`,
   `getLibraryProgram`) are working examples.
2. Write the program. Copy each parameter name from `getEffectDefinition`. Do
   not guess names. `choices` lists accepted values. For a `member` parameter,
   insert its value as a DSL member expression, such as `palette.hypercolor`,
   without quotes.
3. Check it with `validateProgram`. Fix every diagnostic with severity `error`.
4. Run it on a deck with `setProgram`. Look at the result with `getThumbnail`.

```js
const A = window.VisualizeAgent
const dsl = [
    'search synth, filter',
    'let bass = audio(band: 0, min: 0.5, max: 1)',
    'noise(ridges: true, speed: bass).write(o0)',
    'render(o0)',
].join('\n')
const check = await A.validateProgram({ dsl })
if (!check.result.valid) return check.result.diagnostics
const run = await A.setProgram({ dsl, deck: 'B' })
await A.setCrossfader({ position: 1 })
return { ok: run.ok, error: run.error }
```

DSL rules that agents most often get wrong:

- The first line `search ns1, ns2` sets the namespaces that effect names
  resolve in, in order. The same function name can mean different effects in
  different namespaces, with different parameters.
- Every chain ends with `.write(oN)`. The program ends with `render(oN)`.
  Read another surface with `read(oN)`, for example `tex: read(o0)`.
- Older examples use retired parameter names such as `mixAmt`. Those fail with
  `S001 Unknown argument`. `getEffectDefinition` gives the current names.

What is special about programs in Visualize:

- Audio: `let bass = audio(band: 0, min: 0.5, max: 1)` declares a binding;
  use its name as a parameter value. Bands are 0 (low), 1 (mid) and 2 (high).
  `min` and `max` are fractions of the parameter's range, from 0 (its lowest
  value) to 1 (its highest). The engine clamps them to that span and gives no
  diagnostic. The parameter is at the `min` fraction at silence and at the
  `max` fraction at full level. `getEffectDefinition` gives the range. For
  example, `noise` `speed` runs from -100 to 100, so `speed: bass` is 0 at
  silence and 100 at full level. Bindings move
  only while audio input is on (`state.audio.enabled`); the person turns it on.
  `setAudio` sets the input sensitivity. `rebind` rewrites random parameters into
  new `audio()` or `midi()` bindings.
- Oscillators: `let swing = osc(type: oscKind.sine, min: 0.2, max: 1)` moves a
  parameter between the same fractions of its range in time with the deck
  loop, so it follows the tempo.
- Curated programs: library programs in the `curated` section run effects from
  the `curated` namespace (`searchEffects({ namespace: 'curated' })`).
  `getProgram` and `getLibraryProgram` return them with `search curated`. Keep
  that line when you change one.
- User effects: custom effects installed in this browser are in the `user`
  namespace. In the browser, `listUserEffects` lists them and `searchEffects`
  includes them. A session cannot read or run them.
- Images: a deck shows an image with `media(url: "image:<sha256>")`, where the
  id is the SHA-256 of the image bytes. Through a session, add the file with
  `image-put` and use the reference it prints; `transfer` copies images for
  you. The image must be in a deck or in the online session (in the browser,
  also in this browser's scene images); otherwise `setProgram` fails with
  `NOT_FOUND_IMAGE`. Any
  other `url` value (a web link or inline image data) is refused with a
  `MEDIA_URL` diagnostic; through a session, the tab refuses it first with
  `OUTSIDE_LINK` or `IMAGE_AS_TEXT`.

---

## Keep results small

Your tool sends each result back to you. A large result uses a large part of
your context.

- Return only the fields that you need from each script.
- Every envelope includes `state`. Remove it when you do not need it.
- `searchLibrary` and `searchEffects` take `limit`. Library program text comes
  only from `getLibraryProgram`, one program at a time.
- Page JavaScript `getThumbnail` returns base64 image data. Keep
  `maxDimension` small. WebMCP and the Seance route carry the image
  separately and omit its bytes from text.

---

## The envelope

Every command response, success or failure, has this shape:

```js
// success
{ ok: true, command: "setProgram", apiVersion: "1.0", result: { /* command-specific */ }, state: { /* snapshot */ } }

// failure
{
    ok: false,
    command: "setProgram",
    apiVersion: "1.0",
    error: { code: "INVALID_PROGRAM", message: "...", details: { diagnostics: [ /* ... */ ] } },
    state: { /* snapshot */ }
}
```

A success can add `warnings: [ "..." ]`, for example a scene recall that could
not restore everything. Commands run one at a time, in the order you call
them. You can omit the argument object: `getState()` is the same as
`getState({})`. Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, so
a command with no arguments accepts only `{}`.

---

## State snapshot

```
state: {
    schemaVersion,
    decks: {
        A: { title, chars, running, speed, density: { mode, value }, bandpass, oscillators },
        B: { ... }                       // running: the program text is the program that runs
    },
    crossfader: { position, curve, fadeSeconds, live },  // live: "A" or "B"
    mixer:      { effect },              // null until the mixer has started
    fx:         { strobe, invert, bw, zoom, freeze },
    autoVj:     { enabled, bars },
    autoMix:    { enabled, source },     // source such as "osc:sine", "audio:low", "midi:1"
    tempo:      { bpm, divider, followMidiClock },
    audio:      { enabled, sensitivity },
    midi:       { enabled, inputs },
    output:     { width, height, backend },  // backend: "webgl2" or "webgpu"
    recording,
    online                               // "offline", "connecting", "online" or "readonly"
}
```

---

## Diagnostics

`validateProgram` and a failed `setProgram` return compiler diagnostics:

```js
{ code: "S001", severity: "error", message: "Unknown argument 'madeUp' for noise()", location?: { line, column } }
```

A syntax error has code `SYNTAX`. A `media()` image that is not named
`image:<sha256>` has code `MEDIA_URL`. Through a session, a program that names
the `user` namespace anywhere has code `USER_EFFECT`, without saying whether
any user effect exists. Diagnostics with severity
`warning` do not stop a program.

---

## Error codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_ARGS_TYPE` | wrong argument type |
| `INVALID_ARGS_REQUIRED` | missing required argument |
| `INVALID_ARGS_RANGE` | number or string length out of range |
| `INVALID_ARGS_ENUM` | value not in the allowed list |
| `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN` | an argument, or a mixer parameter, that the command does not declare |
| `INVALID_PROGRAM` | the program does not compile. `details.diagnostics` lists the errors. Nothing changed |
| `COMPILE_FAILED` | the renderer rejected a program that passed the compiler. The deck runs its previous program |
| `NOT_FOUND_EFFECT` | unknown effect id, or a `user` effect asked for through a session |
| `EFFECT_LOAD_FAILED` | an effect could not load from the shader CDN |
| `NOT_FOUND_PROGRAM` | no library program has that title (through a session, the `user` section is left out), or the Auto-VJ pool is empty |
| `NOT_FOUND_IMAGE` | a program names an `image:<sha256>` that is not in the deck, the browser or the session |
| `NOT_FOUND_SCENE` | no scene has that name |
| `NOT_FOUND_COMMAND` | unknown command |
| `CONFLICT_SUPERSEDED` | a newer program load on the same deck, from the person or Auto-VJ, replaced yours |
| `CONFLICT_MIXER_UNAVAILABLE` | the mixer did not start; the decks crossfade without a mixer effect |
| `CONFLICT_SCENES_FULL` | the scene list is full. Delete or rename a scene first |
| `CONFLICT_SCENE_EXISTS` | another scene already has the new name |
| `CONFLICT_STORAGE_FULL` | browser storage is full or unavailable; the scene was not saved |
| `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE` | the command runs only in the person's browser, or would reveal live camera or video input |
| `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FAILED` | an image result could not be added to the session |
| `OUTSIDE_LINK` | a session request names media by an outside link. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `IMAGE_AS_TEXT` | a session request or answer would carry an image as base64 text. Add the image with `image-put` and use `image:<sha256>` |
| `IMAGE_LIMIT` | the tab already added 16 images to the session in ten minutes. `details.retryAfter` gives the seconds to wait |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | unexpected failure |

---

## Command reference

Call a command as `await window.VisualizeAgent.<name>(args)`,
as the WebMCP tool `visualize_<name>`, or through a Seance session with `seance-agent.mjs call <name>`.
Every command rejects an argument that it does not declare, with `INVALID_ARGS_UNKNOWN`.

### Read state

#### `getState`

Returns the state snapshot. Every envelope already includes it in `state`. Through a session, a deck's `title`, `chars` and `running` describe the text that the session holds for it.

Returns: the snapshot.

Arguments: none.

#### `getProgram`

Returns the program text of deck `deck`, as its editor shows it, and whether it is the program that runs. Through a session it returns the text that the session holds for the deck: a change shows once the tab has published it, and a draft that stays out of the session does not show. A curated library program reads in the `curated` namespace. An image the program shows is named `image:<sha256>`.

Returns: `{ dsl, running }`.

Arguments:

- `deck`: string, one of `A`, `B`, default `A`

### Programs

#### `validateProgram`

Compiles `dsl` without applying it. Both decks compile a program the same way. Through a session, a program that names the `user` namespace anywhere gets only a `USER_EFFECT` error diagnostic.

Returns: `{ valid, diagnostics }`.

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `setProgram`

Compiles `dsl` and runs it on deck `deck`, like a program typed into that deck's editor. A program that does not compile changes nothing and fails with INVALID_PROGRAM. Each `image:<sha256>` the program names must be in the online session, or, in the browser, in a deck or this browser's scene images. While Visualize is online, the program goes to the session document `deck:A` or `deck:B`.

Returns: `{ applied: true, diagnostics }` (warnings only).

Arguments:

- `dsl` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `deck`: string, one of `A`, `B`, default `A`

### Effects

#### `searchEffects`

Lists effects whose id, description or tags contain `query`. `namespace` keeps one namespace. The list includes the `curated` effects that library programs use and, in the browser only, the `user` effects installed in this browser.

Returns: `{ total, effects: [{ effectId, namespace, name, description, tags }] }`.

Arguments:

- `query`: string
- `namespace`: string
- `limit`: integer, from 1 to 500, default `50`

#### `getEffectDefinition`

Returns the DSL function name and the parameters of one effect. A session cannot read `user` effects.

Returns: `{ effectId, func, namespace, description, params: [{ name, type, default, min?, max?, enum?, choices?, label? }] }`.

Arguments:

- `effectId` (required): string, at least 1 character

### Library

#### `searchLibrary`

Lists library programs whose title, tagline, tags or author contain `query`. `category` keeps one library section: `user`, `curated`, `abstract`, `attractor`, `geometric`, `life`, `particles`, `built-in`, `noiseblaster` or `util`. The `user` section, made from the user effects installed in this browser, is listed only in the browser.

Returns: `{ total, programs: [{ title, tagline, category, tags, autoVj }] }`, where `autoVj` tells whether Auto-VJ and `randomize` can pick the program. Through a session `autoVj` is left out.

Arguments:

- `query`: string
- `category`: string
- `limit`: integer, from 1 to 500, default `50`

#### `getLibraryProgram`

Returns one library program with its DSL text, as a deck editor shows it after the program loads.

Returns: `{ title, tagline, category, tags, autoVj, dsl }`.

Arguments:

- `title` (required): string, at least 1 character

#### `loadProgram`

Loads the library program titled `title` into deck `deck`, like the A or B button on its card.

Returns: `{ deck, title }`.

Arguments:

- `title` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `deck`: string, one of `A`, `B`, default `A`

#### `randomize`

Loads a random program from the Auto-VJ pool into deck `deck`, or into both decks, like the shuffle buttons. A deck gets a different program from the one it runs. Through a session the pick comes from the whole library except utility and `user` programs, not from the person's pool.

Returns: `{ programs }`, the loaded titles by deck, such as `{ A: "..." }`.

Arguments:

- `deck`: string, one of `A`, `B`, `both`, default `A`

#### `setAutoVjPool`

Includes or excludes one library program from the Auto-VJ pool, like the switch on its card. Utility programs are never in the pool.

Returns: `{ title, included }`.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `title` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `included` (required): boolean

### Decks

#### `setDeck`

Changes the controls of deck `deck`. Give only the fields you change. `speed` multiplies the playback speed. `density` is the render resolution of the deck in percent of the output; `auto` renders particle and simulation programs at 50% and other programs at 100%. `bandpass` and `oscillators` shape the next `rebind`: with `bandpass`, an EQ rebind uses only the audio bands that the program is tagged with; `oscillators` is how many of the rebound parameters get an `osc()` instead of `audio()` or `midi()`.

Returns: `{ deck, speed, density: { mode, value }, bandpass, oscillators }`.

Arguments:

- `deck`: string, one of `A`, `B`, default `A`
- `speed`: number, from 0.1 to 4
- `density`: string, one of `auto`, `100`, `75`, `50`, `25`
- `bandpass`: boolean
- `oscillators`: integer, from 0 to 4

#### `rebind`

Reshuffles the audio (`eq`) or MIDI (`midi`) bindings of deck `deck`, like its rebind buttons. Two to four numeric parameters of the program get new `audio()` or `midi()` automations. The program text changes; `getProgram` returns it.

Returns: `{ deck, kind, applied }`, where `applied` is false when the program has no parameter to rebind.

Arguments:

- `deck`: string, one of `A`, `B`, default `A`
- `kind` (required): string, one of `eq`, `midi`

### Crossfader and mixer

#### `setCrossfader`

Moves the crossfader and sets its curve and fade time. Give only the fields you change. `position` 0 shows deck A and 1 shows deck B. Moving it stops a running fade and holds Auto-VJ back for a moment, like the slider. `fadeSeconds` is the duration of `autoFade` and of Auto-VJ transitions.

Returns: `{ position, curve, fadeSeconds, live }`.

Arguments:

- `position`: number, from 0 to 1
- `curve`: string, one of `linear`, `dipped`, `sharp`, `cut`
- `fadeSeconds`: number, from 0.1 to 16

#### `crossfade`

`cutA` and `cutB` jump the crossfader to one deck. `autoFade` fades to the deck that is not live over the fade time. The command returns when the fade starts.

Returns: `{ action, target, seconds }`.

Arguments:

- `action` (required): string, one of `cutA`, `cutB`, `autoFade`

#### `getMixer`

Returns the mixer effect that blends deck A with deck B, the effects you can choose, and the parameters of the current effect. The crossfader drives the parameter named by `driver`; the others are in `params`.

Returns: `{ effect, driver, effects: [{ effect, label, driver }], params: [{ name, type, value, default, min?, max?, choices? }] }`.

Arguments: none.

#### `setMixer`

Selects the mixer effect and sets its parameters, like the mixer picker and the controls under the output. A new `effect` starts from its defaults. `params` maps parameter names from `getMixer` to values: a number in range, or a choice name. An unknown name or a bad value fails the command and changes nothing.

Returns: the same result as `getMixer`.

Arguments:

- `effect`: string, one of `mixer/blendMode`, `mixer/applyMode`, `mixer/centerMask`, `mixer/split`, `mixer/patternMix`, `mixer/shapeMask`
- `params`: object

### Output effects

#### `setFx`

Turns output effects on or off, like the FX buttons. Give only the effects you change. `strobe` flashes white on every beat and can trigger photosensitive epilepsy. `invert`, `bw` (black and white) and `zoom` are display effects on the output canvas. `freeze` holds the current output frame. `flash: true` fires one white flash.

Returns: `{ strobe, invert, bw, zoom, freeze }`.

Arguments:

- `strobe`: boolean
- `invert`: boolean
- `bw`: boolean
- `zoom`: boolean
- `freeze`: boolean
- `flash`: boolean

### Automation

#### `setAutoVj`

Turns Auto-VJ on or off and sets its cycle length in bars: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32. Every cycle, Auto-VJ loads a random pool program into the deck that is not live and fades to it. Turning Auto-VJ on turns Auto-Mix off. The cycle length is also the period of an Auto-Mix oscillator. A session can turn Auto-VJ off and set the cycle, but not turn it on: Auto-VJ draws from the person's stored pool.

Returns: `{ enabled, bars }`.

Arguments:

- `enabled`: boolean
- `bars`: integer, one of `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16`, `32`, from 1 to 32

#### `setAutoMix`

Turns Auto-Mix on or off and sets its source. Auto-Mix moves the crossfader from one source: an oscillator with one period per cycle, an audio band level, or the last control change on a MIDI channel. Turning Auto-Mix on turns Auto-VJ off.

Returns: `{ enabled, source }`.

Arguments:

- `enabled`: boolean
- `source`: string, one of `osc:sine`, `osc:tri`, `osc:saw`, `osc:sawInv`, `osc:square`, `audio:sub`, `audio:low`, `audio:mid`, `audio:high`, `midi:1`, `midi:2`, `midi:3`, `midi:4`, `midi:5`, `midi:6`, `midi:7`, `midi:8`, `midi:9`, `midi:10`, `midi:11`, `midi:12`, `midi:13`, `midi:14`, `midi:15`, `midi:16`

### Tempo, audio and output

#### `setTempo`

Sets the tempo, like the tempo bar. Give only the fields you change. `bpm` is beats per minute. `divider` is the number of bars in one deck loop: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32. `tap: true` taps the tempo once; taps less than two seconds apart set the BPM from their spacing. `resetPhase: true` starts the bar now. With `followMidiClock`, an incoming MIDI clock sets the BPM.

Returns: `{ bpm, divider, followMidiClock }`.

Arguments:

- `bpm`: number, from 40 to 300
- `divider`: integer, one of `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16`, `32`, from 1 to 32
- `tap`: boolean
- `resetPhase`: boolean
- `followMidiClock`: boolean

#### `setAudio`

Sets the audio sensitivity, the gain applied to the person's audio input before its levels drive `audio()` bindings and Auto-Mix. The browser stores it.

Returns: `{ enabled, sensitivity }`.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `sensitivity`: number, from 0.5 to 4

#### `setOutput`

Sets the output resolution of both decks, the mixer and the output canvas.

Returns: `{ width, height, backend }`.

Arguments:

- `resolution`: string, one of `640x360`, `1280x720`, `1920x1080`, `2560x1440`

#### `setRenderer`

Stores whether this browser prefers WebGPU to WebGL2. It takes effect when the page reloads.

Returns: `{ preferWebGPU, backend }`, where `backend` is the renderer that runs now.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `preferWebGPU` (required): boolean

### Scenes

#### `listScenes`

Lists the saved scenes in slot order. Shift with the slot number recalls slots 1 to 9.

Returns: `{ total, max, scenes: [{ slot, name, bpm, fx, decks: { A, B } }] }`, with the program titles of the decks and the names of the active effects.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments: none.

#### `scene`

`save` stores the state of both decks, the crossfader, tempo, effects, mixer and automation as scene `name`, and replaces a scene with that name. `recall` restores scene `name`. `rename` gives scene `name` the name `newName`. `delete` removes scene `name` without a confirmation. Scenes are stored in this browser.

Returns: `{ action, name }`, plus `newName` for `rename`. A recall that could not restore everything lists the problems in `warnings`.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `action` (required): string, one of `save`, `recall`, `rename`, `delete`
- `name` (required): string, at least 1 character
- `newName`: string, at least 1 character

### User effects

#### `listUserEffects`

Lists the custom effects installed in this browser. Programs call them in the `user` namespace.

Returns: `{ total, effects: [{ effectId, name, installedAt }] }`.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments: none.

### Images

#### `getThumbnail`

Returns an image of the output canvas, or with `source` of one deck canvas. The output image shows the mix, strobe and flash. It does not show `invert`, `bw` and `zoom`, which are display effects on the canvas element. Through a Seance session the image is added to the session as its own bytes, and `image` replaces `bytes`; a session cannot take an image of a deck that can show live camera or video pixels, of the output while either deck can, or of an output that froze while one could (`REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Returns: `{ bytes, mimeType, width, height, source }`, with `bytes` in base64. Through a session: `{ image: { id, mimeType, bytes }, mimeType, width, height, source }`, where `image.bytes` is the byte count.

Arguments:

- `maxDimension`: integer, from 16 to 1024, default `256`
- `format`: string, one of `png`, `jpg`, default `jpg`
- `source`: string, one of `output`, `A`, `B`, default `output`

### Inputs and recording

#### `setAudioInput`

Turns audio input on with the default device, or off, like the audio button in the status bar. Turning it on asks the person for microphone permission.

Returns: `{ enabled }`, false when the person refused permission.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `enabled` (required): boolean

#### `setMidiInput`

Turns MIDI input on or off, like the MIDI button in the status bar. Turning it on asks the person for MIDI permission.

Returns: `{ enabled, inputs }`.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `enabled` (required): boolean

#### `record`

Starts or stops recording the output, like the record button. Stopping saves the recording as a browser download.

Returns: `{ recording }`.

Browser only: through a Seance session it fails with `REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Arguments:

- `recording` (required): boolean
